artworks.title: Farnese Hercules
artworks.artist: After Lysippos (signed by Glykon of Athens)
artworks.year: c. 216 CE (Roman copy after a 4th-century BCE Greek original)
artworks.description: The colossal exhausted hero leaning on his club with the Nemean lion-skin and the apples of the Hesperides behind his back — the canonical image of the Twelve Labours complete.

artworks.title: The Choice of Hercules
artworks.description: Carracci's Farnese Camerino painting of Virtue and Pleasure offering the young Alcides his path — the moral crossroads before the labours and the wide wars.

artworks.title: Heracles and the Nemean Lion, metope from the Temple of Zeus at Olympia
artworks.artist: Unknown (workshop of the Temple of Zeus, Olympia)
artworks.description: Olympia's metope opens the Labours — the weary hero after the Nemean Lion, Athena looking on in Severe-style calm.

artworks.title: Heracles Strangling the Serpents (detail of an Attic red-figure stamnos)
artworks.description: The cradle miracle that opens the cycle — infant Heracles throttling Hera's serpents while Iphicles recoils.

artworks.title: Hercules and the Lernaean Hydra
artworks.description: Moreau's Symbolist Hydra — the second Labour as jewelled nightmare, the many-headed marsh beast of the Heracles cycle.
